::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 15th 1880  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Columbia University Library, New York:  Harper Bros Collection
:::

Messrs [Harper](people/person_248.qmd)

I am much obliged for the [£10](organizations/other_160.qmd) for [Love and Life](cmy_books/cmybook_137.qmd) received on the 14th yesterday. I am also much obliged to you for sending me your ‘[paper for young people](organizations/other_250.qmd).’[^1] I ventured to extract a short poem on the Plumes of Crecy for a [Reading Book for schools](cmy_books/cmybook_150.qmd) making however a few alterations to bring it more into accordance with history than romance[^2]

Yours faithfully
C.M. Yonge

---

[^1]: There is a pencil line beside the mention of the reading book and  ‘Is not this worth mention?’ written in pencil. Underneath, in ink ‘Attended to./ S.S.C.’
[^2]: Lillie E. Barr, ‘The Plumes of Creçy’ was included in *English History Reading Books* III, 106-9, with a note ‘in Harper’s Young People (slightly altered)’.  CMY has reciprocated the American [piracy](organizations/other_172.qmd) of her work.
